role: Senior Manager, Analytics Engineering and Data Strategy - Technology Business Enablement
responsibilities: Lead the design and development of trusted, analytics-ready data foundations that transform complex enterprise and workforce data into reusable, business-ready datasets

Lead discovery across complex or fragmented workforce data domains to understand source systems, business definitions, data grain, keys, history, dependencies, quality considerations, and downstream consumption needs
Design scalable data models, transformation layers, and architectures that support workforce metrics, reporting, advanced analytics, and AI
Establish consistent approaches to business rules, historical data, reusable dimensions, data quality, and lineage
Partner with business and technical stakeholders to translate analytical needs into scalable, reusable data products rather than one-off solutions
Define data-product architecture, transformations, business logic, quality standards, documentation, and ownership
Balance immediate business priorities with long-term architectural scalability, maintainability, and reuse
Lead hands-on development of complex data transformations using SQL, BigQuery, and Python, leveraging tools such as dbt, Git, and Apache Airflow or comparable technologies
Establish engineering standards for modular development, version control, testing, deployment, orchestration, and monitoring
Implement automated data-quality, validation, reconciliation, and lineage capabilities to improve trust and reliability
Serve as a technical bridge across Business, Analytics, Data Engineering, Architecture, Governance, and enterprise technology teams
Shape the analytics engineering and workforce data strategy, identifying opportunities to simplify fragmented data ecosystems and build scalable capabilities
Enable reliable data consumption across Power BI, Excel, SQL, Python, and emerging AI solutions
Mentor team members and promote engineering practices focused on reusability, automation, quality, and business value
Mentor and upskill analysts and other team members in SQL, data modeling, data-product thinking, reusable transformation patterns, data quality, and modern analytical development practices
Promote a data product mindset centered on business value, reliability, reusability, maintainability, automation, quality, and ownership

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Implement automated data-quality, validation, reconciliation, and lineage capabilities to improve trust and reliability
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Quality, governance, lineage and testing language runs through every section and there is no speed language, so rigour: "Implement automated data-quality, validation, reconciliation, and lineage capabilities to improve trust and reliability".
evidence.domain_risk: deliver forward-looking, data-driven insights on workforce planning, organizational design, and location strategy
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The employer is a bank, but the data is technology workforce planning with no financial reporting or regulatory language, so the sector tie-breaker gives moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: ETS Portfolio; ETS Finance; Talent Acquisitions; Global Real Estate; Technology Vendor Management; Data Engineering; Architecture; Data Governance; Analytics
evidence.data_team_maturity: help move WFS from fragmented, report-specific data preparation toward a governed analytics ecosystem
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Analysts, data engineering, architecture and governance teams already exist, and the role improves a fragmented setup rather than founding one: "help move WFS from fragmented, report-specific data preparation toward a governed analytics ecosystem".
evidence.jd_authorship: Lead discovery across complex or fragmented workforce data domains to understand source systems, business definitions, data grain, keys, history, dependencies
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Some bullets are precise about grain, keys and the SQL, BigQuery, dbt and Airflow stack, while others are generic, such as "Balance immediate business priorities with long-term architectural scalability".
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: enabling analysts and business teams to spend less time sourcing, joining, cleaning, and reconciling data
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary consumers are the workforce strategy analysts who use the reusable data products: "enabling analysts and business teams to spend less time sourcing, joining, cleaning, and reconciling data".
evidence.autonomy_level: Shape the analytics engineering and workforce data strategy
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role sets strategy and standards for the domain: "Shape the analytics engineering and workforce data strategy" and "Establish engineering standards".
evidence.ai_role: Design scalable data models, transformation layers, and architectures that support workforce metrics, reporting, advanced analytics, and AI
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds data foundations that AI consumes, named in the responsibilities rather than only the company description.
evidence.testing_framing: Establish engineering standards for modular development, version control, testing, deployment, orchestration, and monitoring
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and automated data quality are framed as standards the candidate establishes and implements.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Lead the design and development of trusted, analytics-ready data foundations
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Trust is the opening responsibility and recurs throughout (trusted, governed, reconciliation, lineage), so the register is high: the fear is untrusted data reaching decision-makers.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: identifying opportunities to simplify fragmented data ecosystems and build scalable capabilities
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role both establishes new data foundations and simplifies a fragmented existing setup, so mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: "The Sr. Manager, Analytics Engineering and Data Strategy will lead the development of scalable analytics data foundations and reusable data products" — framed around trusted, governed and reconciled data throughout.
